iconicAnchor.label: Museum design monograph and collection publication systems
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Museum curators, editors, designers, and collection photographers
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The Met publication model establishes a sustained visual argument through object plates, scholarly sequencing, catalog information, and close reproductions rather than treating a designed object as a single advertising hero.

sources.title: The Painterly Print: Monotypes from the Seventeenth to the Twentieth Century
supports: The museum publication demonstrates how a monograph combines visual plates, sustained scholarship, and catalog structure.
The publication record supports object-centered sequencing rather than isolated lifestyle imagery.

sources.title: Design Journal, Spring/Summer 2017
supports: The institutional journal shows disciplined layouts for designed objects, captions, essays, and supporting detail images.
Its spreads support repeated-view logic, controlled scale changes, and a coherent publication grid.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches object plates, repeated views, caption discipline, dimensions, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/design-monograph/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
